review_comments.body: Can we add a test for ingress update case too ? Right now only egress is tested, so if ingress maps are missed in the close list tests still pass. Lets also add per pod maps and conntrack map to the ingress entry here so we catch if we close FDs of the entry we keep. Map key should be map name (aws_conntrack_map) and not the pin path. We can also check egressPgmInfo is empty in the stored context

Thanks for these changes

This test mocks the SDK, so we won't catch it if SDK changes how these FDs are opened or how maps are keyed. Can we add a kernel test in pkg/ebpf which loads real ingress and egress programs, runs recoverBPFState with updateEgressProbe=true and checks FD count does not increase ? Can you also share the FD count on a node with this fix ?

Thanks for the review. Pushed a test-only follow-up:
- Added `TestRecoverBPFStateClosesFDsOfUpdatedIngress`: with updateIngressProbe=true only the ingress program and per-pod map FDs are closed. Both this test and the egress one now give the kept entry per-pod maps (ingress or egress map, cluster-policy map, pod state map) plus `aws_conntrack_map`, so closing the kept entry's FDs, or leaving a map out of the close list, fails the assertions. It fails with the `closeRecoveredPodFDs` call removed.
- The conntrack map is now keyed by map name (`aws_conntrack_map`) in both tests, and both assert the replaced direction's stored context is empty.
- Not done yet: the kernel test (load real ingress/egress programs, run `recoverBPFState` with `updateEgressProbe=true`, compare FD counts) and an FD count from a node. Both need root and a node, which this follow-up was not tested on. A kernel test along the lines of `tcp_reset_kernel_test.go` (skips under `make test`, runs in the nightly kernel job) can follow if that works for you.

This comment was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code) and the change is covered by unit tests only.
